title: LangChain overview
text: create_agent is the high-level entry point for building agents in LangChain. It takes a model, a list of tools, and optional instructions, and returns a compiled agent that can be invoked with messages. LangGraph is the lower-level runtime underneath it.

title: LangChain agents guide
text: An agent is created with create_agent(model, tools, system_prompt). Invoke it with a message dict containing a 'human' role. The response contains an 'ai' message. Tools are plain Python functions; a docstring becomes the tool description the model uses to decide whether to call it.

title: LangChain tools guide
text: Any Python callable can be a tool. @tool decorates a function and derives its schema from the type hints and docstring. When a tool needs a live capability -- a database, an HTTP endpoint, the filesystem -- the plain function is called inside a ToolNode, which is what lets the model's tool choice reach real code.

title: LangChain persistence and short-term memory
text: Short-term memory keeps one conversation. Pass a thread_id in the config to invoke so state is scoped to that thread and can be recovered between calls. Checkpointer implementations include InMemorySaver for a single process and SqliteSaver or PostgresSaver to survive a restart.

title: LangChain retrieval guide
text: A retrieval tool wraps a retriever as a callable the agent can choose. Split documents into overlapping chunks, embed them, and store them in a vector store. The agent decides when the question needs external knowledge, which is the difference from a pipeline that always retrieves.

title: LangChain middleware guide
text: Middleware wraps agent execution to add control: guardrails, retries, human approval, summarisation, or custom logging. Middleware is passed to create_agent as a list. Ordering matters -- an outer middleware sees the request first and the response last.
